messages:
Rachel Kim: starting a thread on beta customer selection for Dedicated staged rollouts. we need 2 (maybe 3) dedicated tenants for the first wave. criteria: high SLA sensitivity + willingness to do enablement + can tolerate feature-flagged behavior + has had pain w current “pool-level all-at-once”

Miguel Santos: +1. from the last quarter escalations, top pain came from customers with reserved pools running close to headroom already. but that’s also our risk… we should pick ones with enough steady traffic to validate gates, but not “always redlining”

Dev Patel: support POV: we should bias toward customers who (a) have reliable SRE contacts and (b) won’t open 10 tickets for expected “pause/hold” behavior. we’ll need clean comms about “hold is safe / not broken”

Rachel Kim: proposed shortlist based on account notes + SUP tickets:
1) Northbridge Health (Dedicated, compliance-heavy, asked for audit trail; ties to SUP-3981)
2) VantagePay (Dedicated, had rollout latency spike; similar to SUP-3917 pattern)
3) LatticeWorks (Dedicated mid-enterprise, good eng partner, less compliance)

Miguel Santos: Northbridge is super engaged but they’re strict on change mgmt. if we don’t have audit exports working end-to-end they may block. do we have the audit events in beta or is that GA?

Marissa Cole: audit events are in beta scope (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold). export pipeline is “best effort” initially but we can provide in-console audit log + API pagination. Marcus/Kevin are tracking retention/export improvements, but I’d be careful promising SIEM export on day 1

Lauren Bishop: for Dedicated specifically, we need at least one customer that does model updates weekly-ish. otherwise we won’t learn anything about the stage gates and approval workflow. VantagePay changes more often than Northbridge

Sean Gallagher: SRE take: I’m ok with 2 customers max for first beta wave. we’re still tuning evaluator lag + “missing metrics => pause” behavior. if we pick a customer with spotty telemetry we’ll spend the whole beta chasing “perpetual hold”

Rachel Kim: agree. so maybe wave 1 = VantagePay + LatticeWorks? and Northbridge as wave 2 once audit logging + docs are more polished?

Miguel Santos: i like that split. Northbridge also wants written governance language (“who can approve”, “what happens on hold/rollback”). we can prep a tighter enablement deck and get them in wave 2

Dev Patel: if VantagePay is wave 1, can we set expectations on support path? i’d like an explicit escalation: #dedicated-rollouts-beta (private) + oncall alias, and we tell them “don’t file tickets unless production impact.” otherwise my queue will be spammed

Lauren Bishop: we can do a shared Slack connect channel with VantagePay if they want. but for beta I’d rather keep it email + scheduled check-ins unless there’s an incident

Marissa Cole: for comms, we should send:
- 1-pager: what staged rollouts are (deterministic stages), what gates we evaluate, what “hold” means
- limitations: v1 is operator-driven, no customer self-serve for editing stages, and quality gates are optional
- what we need from them: a “golden route” to observe, baseline SLO targets, and a change window

Rachel Kim: success criteria proposal (tell me if this is too much):
1) customer can run at least 2 real rollouts using stages (5% -> 25% -> 100%)
2) at least 1 gate failure triggers safe hold (no SLA breach) and rollback path is clear
3) approvals + audit trail meets their internal change mgmt needs (at least in-console / API)
4) no more than 1 P1 support escalation caused by rollout tooling

Sean Gallagher: i’d tweak #2: “gate failure triggers hold before customer-visible impact” is the aspiration, but we should define measurable thresholds. ex: “no sustained p95 latency regression > X% for > Y minutes” during a rollout. also: we need a defined “metrics freshness” requirement or we’ll debate every hold event

Miguel Santos: also add a “time to diagnose” goal. today when a model update goes bad, they and we flail. with the stage detail + gate view, they should be able to see WHY it paused (p95 vs 5xx vs queue depth) in <10 min

Dev Patel: +1. and document what’s expected: if it pauses at stage 1, do we auto-rollback or require manual abort? customers will ask

Marissa Cole: current behavior (beta): gate fail => automatic HOLD. rollback is manual via abort (operator action) unless SRE flips the “auto-rollback on hard fail” flag. we can keep auto-rollback disabled in wave 1 to reduce surprise

Lauren Bishop: risks we should explicitly call out to the customers:
- partial stage allocation can create uneven utilization if they have multiple routes pinned to the same pool
- capacity headroom: stage traffic shift can temporarily spike queue depth
- missing/late metrics => hold (safe but can slow down change)

Rachel Kim: ok. enablement plan:
- kickoff (45 min) with customer eng lead + ops lead
- we run first rollout with them in a maintenance window
- weekly 30 min check-in for 4 weeks, plus async notes
- shared doc with “what to do if paused”, and who to page

Sean Gallagher: pls include “if paused: don’t keep retrying rollout actions.” we saw racey behavior when folks spam approve/abort. it’s better now but still…

Dev Patel: and pls include “if you see hold due to missing metrics, contact us with timestamps + pool_id” (and we’ll check evaluator lag dashboards). otherwise we get vague reports

Miguel Santos: about customers: I can confirm VantagePay is willing. they asked last month for “5% canary” specifically. their eng manager is responsive

Rachel Kim: LatticeWorks?

Miguel Santos: yes, they’re lower risk and good partners. they don’t have strict compliance needs so we can iterate faster

Lauren Bishop: for wave 1 we should ensure both are on Dedicated pools with the new routing bits enabled (the deterministic stage allocation). we’ll need to coordinate with Ethan/Mina’s team on allowlisting tenant ids

Marissa Cole: I’ll sync with Talia on timeline + get a draft customer-facing one-pager into review. Kenji has some screenshots for the stage list + gate badges we can include

Talia Benson: jumping in — for scheduling, I can hold slots the week after next for 2 kickoffs. if we pick VantagePay + LatticeWorks, I’ll propose Tues/Thu and share an agenda + pre-read

Rachel Kim: great. action items:
- Rachel: confirm customer contacts + send “beta invite” email template
- Miguel: validate technical fit (pool type, expected traffic patterns)
- Marissa: one-pager + screenshots + limitations
- Sean/Dev: escalation path + what we commit to during beta (support hours / oncall)

Dev Patel: works. one more request: we should add a line in the invite about “beta feature, may pause more often than expected, this is by design.” sets expectations

Sean Gallagher: +1. and please don’t call it “automatic rollback” in comms. it’s “automatic hold”

Rachel Kim: noted. I’ll draft comms with that exact wording

Miguel Santos: :thumbsup: wave 2: keep Northbridge warm, but tell them we’re prioritizing stabilizing + audit/export polish first

Rachel Kim: yep. I’ll reply to their last email with that framing + offer to do a preview once we have the audit log screen ready
